html:
Kolmanskop is a ghost town in the Namib desert of southern Namibia, 10 km inland from the port of Lüderitz. It was the boom town of a diamond rush that began in 1908 and was abandoned to the sand by the 1950s.

In 1908 a railway worker, Zacharias Lewala, picked up a diamond near the line and showed it to his German supervisor. The colony of German South West Africa was soon swept by a rush, and the government closed off a huge stretch of desert, the Sperrgebiet or "forbidden zone", to keep the diamonds for licensed companies. This came only a few years after the genocide of the Herero and Nama in the same colony.

The German miners built a little European town in the dunes, with stone houses, a hospital, a ballroom, a skittle alley and an ice factory. African contract workers did the digging. After the First World War richer deposits were found far to the south, and the mines moved; the last people left in 1956. The sand has filled the houses, and the town is now a tourist site run by Namdeb, a joint company of the Namibian government and De Beers.
